We would have two questions to someone from sig-windows or the Kubernetes team:

1. The test container for the device plugin would have additional dependencies:
    https://github.com/StackExchange/wmi
    https://github.com/go-ole/go-ole
    And possibly other indirect dependencies.
    We see the following options:
    - Include these packages into the vendor directory.
      Advantage: Code for building the container is included in the Kubernetes project.
      Disadvantage: Additional stuff in the vendor directory.
    - Don't include the source for the container into the Kubernetes project, as suggested in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93948#issuecomment-673493175.
      Advantage: No extra stuff in the Kubernetes project.
      Disadvantage: The Kubernetes project is not self-contained: It does not contain everything which is necessary to run tests.
    - Reduce the test container to contain only a fake device plugin.
      And reduce the device plugin test to not check the GPU access.
      Advantage: Simplification.
      Disadvantage: We don't verify GPU access. We don't really verify the functionality of device plugins.
      Specifically, it wouldn't make sense anymore to execute dxdiag in the container to verify GPU access:
      https://github.com/Kerstin08/kubernetes_device_plugin_e2e_test/blob/master/test/e2e/windows/device_plugin.go#L119

1. No nodeport needed. 
2. But create and get a device plugin pod similar to the function `getSampleDevicePluginPod` in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/device_plugin_test.go#L82-L99.

please connect with @claudiubelu and @adelina-t for some blueprints on tests for windows

1. Prepare a device plugin test pod image containing https://github.com/aarnaud/k8s-directx-device-plugin.

2. Use the test https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e/windows/service.go as starting point.

I find it's much cleaner to have everything we need contained in the test code.

Thanks, @adelina-t!

We created a fork for the Windows device plugin e2e tests at https://github.com/Kerstin08/kubernetes_device_plugin_e2e_test.

May I ask you the following?

We don't understand https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/device_plugin_test.go#L89-L96.
It seems to create a daemon set, but returns a specific pod. Does this code automatically return the (first?) pod created implicitly by the daemon set?
And how would this code look like when not using a yaml file, but when creating it directly as you recommended?

Other question:
What is the procedure for creating a pod image for testing?

Hm, I don't think it creates a daemon set at all. It just uses reads the daemonSet spec from the file and uses that to fill in the create the pod spec it returns. In turn, you can see it creates that pod here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/device_plugin_test.go#L133 . It specifically creates a pod, no mention of a daemonSet creation. But this is just at first glance.

For the test image, all test images code is here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/897dc66b0e017426d8f2182c4ddcb61dd7ddd93f/test/images

You can add a Dockerfile for a new image here, or you can use one of the existing images if that would work. For example, the agnhost image ( here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/897dc66b0e017426d8f2182c4ddcb61dd7ddd93f/test/images/agnhost ), which is supported by both linux & windows is where we add all sorts of functionality that we need in testing. It's basically the swiss army knife for e2e, it does everything from generating logs to being a simple webserver. You can easily add something else here. 

As for the building process, it's done by hand for the moment for Windows. In general building is done by an image promoter job, @claudiubelu  is adding support for Windows in said image promoter.

Since, from our understanding, a daemonSet is the normal way of creating device plugins, why is this test not using a daemonSet?
What approach should be use for our e2e test?
Our assumption was to create a daemonSet (as we are doing for our real use-cases).
Or would you suggest to use the approach of directly creating a device plugin pod without using a daemonSet as done in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/device_plugin_test.go?

I don't really understand why they designed the test the way they did. I suspect it's because it's just simpler to use a pod. However, a test should be an automation of a real world, so if usage in real use-cases says DaemonSet, you can do that.
Do you by chance have sample code around for creating a DaemonSet?

Look at what I liked above: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a097243cbae780f5e2dadc4630f4204fc6500f97/test/e2e/apps/daemon_set.go#L183-L184 . It's from the daemonSet e2e tests. You can follow the `newDaemonSet` function from there to see exactly what it does and find the object definition for the daemonSet.

Yes, indeed, we should have found that by ourselves. 
Thanks!

Thanks a lot for the help!

May I ask another question?
When having created a busybox test pod as in 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a5b89b8e3c533923cdcb7d85abe53dc601ebed7e/test/e2e/windows/device_plugin.go#L64-L65
is it easily possible to run a command inside the pod which writes a file and then verify the content of that file?

In our case we want to run
```
dxdiag /t dxdiag_output.txt

```
inside the pod and verify that the generated file `dxdiag_output.txt` contains the line
```
          DirectX Version: DirectX 12
```
You can do something like this: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/edbbb6a89f9583f18051218b1adef1def1b777ae/test/e2e/node/kubelet.go#L110

@adelina-t 

My colleague @Kerstin08 created a first implementation of the e2e test:
https://github.com/Kerstin08/kubernetes_device_plugin_e2e_test
It is not tested yet, because we don't know how to setup the e2e testing environment.
Any feedback so far?

It is possible to run that new test directly in the Kubernetes GitHub test infrastructure by this test robot via "/test something"?
If yes, what is necessary for doing this?

There is some documentation on running with kubetest in relation to windows: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-testing#running-an-e2e-test-pass.  If you have questions and possible improvements for that document for new folks that would be helpful.

We can add a test for this in this area: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e/windows

> There is some documentation on running with kubetest in relation to windows: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-testing#running-an-e2e-test-pass. If you have questions and possible improvements for that document for new folks that would be helpful.

Thanks!

> We can add a test for this in this area: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e/windows

Yes, this is where we already put it, see https://github.com/Kerstin08/kubernetes_device_plugin_e2e_test.
